startup.name: Didit
startup.description: Didit sells one API for KYC, KYB, AML screening, authentication, biometrics and fraud signals, with pay as you go pricing and a free tier. Customers are fintechs, marketplaces and any company that must verify users. A team of 20 based in Spain, Winter 2026 batch.

yc_acceptance.basis: Blind test: the company is known to have been accepted, so this is a placeholder note and not a real estimate. The prior for a random applicant is about 1 percent (references/yc_acceptance.md), and this team would sit at the upper end within that range.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: Not applicable in this test because the company was accepted. If YC had said no, the likely reasons would be a crowded identity verification market led by Persona, Sumsub, Veriff and Onfido, plus a lack of a clear wedge that separates a 20 person team from them.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --industry B2B --calibration-only gave seed 59% known only (lower 49%, upper 65%, n=126, median 7 months); Fintech 2020-2024 gave 70% (n=33).
anchors.adjustment_reason: Above the 0.59 anchor but within the Fintech anchor of 70%: a 20 person team already shipping a priced API with a free tier is far further along than the median YC company, and compliance infrastructure raises easily.

bands.rationale: Small seed, similar to the 2022+ B2B median of $3.2M at the low end.
Typical 2022+ seed for fintech infrastructure, near the B2B p50 to p75 of $3.2M to $5M.
Upside with a lead from a fintech fund after strong usage growth.
Thin round from angels and a European fund near the YC cap.

ladder.why_it_fails: The main way this stalls is that investors read it as one more KYC wrapper without a defensible edge, since Authologic, Dojah, Prembly and AiPrise all pitched similar stories after YC and only some raised a priced round. A seed above $500K within a year also needs revenue proof, and pay as you go plus a free tier may show usage without enough revenue to convince leads.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --industry B2B --calibration-only gave series_a 15% known only and 26% given seed (n=74); the 2018-2022 B2B cohort gave 31% given seed (n=74).
anchors.adjustment_reason: About 1.15 times the 2022-2025 conditional anchor of 26% and in line with the 31% for 2018-2022. A team of 20 at batch start suggests existing traction, and identity is a regulated, paid need, balanced by heavy competition.

bands.rationale: Lower Series A for a European compliance infrastructure company.
Median 2022+ B2B Series A of $15M, with revenue growing through regulated customers.
Upside if usage scales across several verticals for a fintech identity API given the stage benchmarks and cohort round sizes.
Thin A or extension if growth is slower.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series A fails when per verification pricing compresses against Persona, Sumsub and Veriff and the company cannot show net revenue retention above the market. Berbix (S18) reached a Series A and was then acquired, and Invoid (W21) was acquired after a seed, which shows many in this category end in small exits instead. Without clear dollars of recurring revenue, a lead will pass.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2018-2022 --industry B2B --calibration-only gave series_b 35% given series_a (n=23); the 2022-2025 B2B cohort gave 16% (n=19).
anchors.adjustment_reason: 0.8 times the higher anchor and 1.75 times the lower, so the middle is used. Both cohorts are small.

bands.rationale: Modest B on strong but not hypergrowth revenue.
Median 2022+ Series B of about $37M to $45M.
Upside if the platform becomes the default for AI native fintechs.
Down or flat round from price pressure for a fintech identity API given the stage benchmarks and cohort round sizes.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series B fails when identity becomes a commodity priced per check and incumbents with larger data networks undercut a 20 to 60 person company. Persona raised a Series D and Sumsub and Veriff have deep pockets, so a late entrant needs a distinct data asset or a regional edge. AiPrise and Authologic reached A but not clearly B.

anchors.source: stage_benchmarks.md gives series_c given B 36% (n=55); B2B 2018-2022 gave 50% (n=8).
anchors.adjustment_reason: Slightly below the anchor to reflect a commodity pricing risk.

bands.rationale: Typical 2022+ Series C near the $45M median.
Growth round on global coverage for a fintech identity API given the stage benchmarks and cohort round sizes.
Upside if it takes share from legacy vendors.
Smaller structured round or strategic investment for a fintech identity API given the stage benchmarks and cohort round sizes.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C fails if growth slows and the company is acquired by a payments or banking infrastructure firm before needing a large round. Cognito (S14) and Berbix (S18) were both acquired in this category, so an acquisition under $1B is the common destination and a large independent growth round is rare.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Failure here mostly means price compression and a stall after a seed, as seen with Invoid and Dojah, which did not show later priced rounds in the data. B2B 2018-2022 had 25% shutdowns and 21% acquisitions, so a meaningful share of this category ends small or quietly.

analogs.outcome_summary: Active with no priced round recorded.

killers.risk: Commodity pricing and incumbents such as Persona, Sumsub and Veriff compress margins
killers.evidence: Persona has raised a reported $200M Series D and Sumsub and Veriff are scaled, so a pay as you go API faces price competition.
killers.mitigation: Win a vertical or region, bundle fraud signals and AML, and keep price per check above cost.

killers.risk: Breadth across KYC, KYB, AML and fraud spreads a 20 person team thin
killers.evidence: The description claims 1,000 data sources and 200 signals, which is wide for a small team and invites quality gaps.
killers.mitigation: Focus on one flagship flow and prove accuracy.

killers.risk: Regulation and sales cycles in banks slow revenue
killers.evidence: Compliance buyers need audits and certifications, which slow enterprise deals.
killers.mitigation: Sell to fintech startups first and collect certifications early.

competition_now.name: Sumsub
competition_now.what: KYC, KYB and AML platform in 220 plus countries.

technical_complexity.rationale: Document and face checks, data source integrations and fraud models are buildable by a 20 person team using existing models. Global coverage and regulatory certification are the harder parts and need years.

takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbents and payment platforms already offer overlapping products and can bundle them for free to protect payments volume, so the product can be copied in months.

evidence.claim: Many vendors compete and Persona raised a large Series D, showing sustained spending on identity verification.
Directories list dozens of paid KYC API providers with per check pricing.

roadmap.goal: A live product with paying users.
actions: Launch the free tier and track conversion.
Win one vertical such as crypto or neobanks.
roadmap.proof: First $500K of annualized revenue and a seed above $500K.
About $2M to $3M annualized revenue with net revenue retention above 100%.
Revenue above $30M and a defensible data asset.

pros.evidence: Persona, Sumsub and Veriff have raised large rounds, so buyers pay for identity verification.

pros.point: A 20 person team with a priced product at batch start
pros.evidence: Team size 20 and a free tier plus pay as you go pricing indicate traction well beyond a typical batch company.

brand.name: Didit
strengths: Short, friendly and easy to say
weaknesses: Does not signal identity or security; resembles a common phrase
brand.rationale: A short playful name that is easy to remember, like many successful YC infrastructure brands, but it says nothing about identity. Effect is mildly positive.

narrative.headline: A well staffed KYC API in a crowded but paying market that likely reaches a seed.
narrative.general_summary: Didit is a 20 person team selling a broad identity and fraud API with pay as you go pricing. Identity verification is a proven paid need, which supports a seed above $500K within a year, and several YC peers such as Authologic and AiPrise reached Series A. The category is crowded and price competition is real, and two close analogs, Berbix and Invoid, ended in acquisitions. Later rounds are therefore plausible but far from assured, and a small acquisition is the most common good outcome. Reaching a round years later is common for companies with paying customers.

assumptions: Blind test using only the batch start description.
B2B and Fintech cohorts used for base rates.
Seed means a round above $500K within about 12 months.
Coverage per knowledge/coverage.md: 662 of 6,399 companies researched.
